incident.location_detail: security desk / ID check, queueing with 41 other arrivals
incident.evidence_of_threat: Guest report claims a vampire in the lobby asking to be let in. Cam E-2 shows one adult in a floor-length black cape, white face paint and plastic fangs, badge B-0061, queueing at the security desk behind 41 other arrivals. He bowed and said 'may I enter?' when the guard waved him through. IR skin reading 33.8C against 21C ambient. EMF 2 mG. Window lux 18,200 with sun on the lobby floor and sunset in 415 min. 212 motion events in 10 min.
incident.ordinary_explanation: Costumed attendee or promoter in a vampire costume (cape, face paint, plastic fangs) with a valid event badge, moving through the normal arrival queue and being waved through by the guard. Skin temperature 33.8C is consistent with a living human in direct sun (lux 18,200) and is not consistent with a cold-blooded undead body. EMF 2 mG is ordinary background. Motion events are consistent with a busy arrival queue.
incident.summary: A costumed attendee in a vampire outfit (cape, face paint, plastic fangs), badge B-0061, was waved through the entrance security desk by the guard. IR skin reading 33.8C in direct sun, EMF 2 mG, and 212 motion events in 10 min are all consistent with a living human in a busy arrival queue. No supernatural indicators; no threat to hold the line.

incident.location_detail: Freight lift to 2nd floor; crates addressed to 'Evening Shift Events, stage plinths'; porter intends to park all three crates in the lounge
incident.evidence_of_threat: Three wooden crates of 2.1 m length weighing 241 kg, 38 kg and 36 kg against a manifest of 35 kg each; black wax on the lids; dark soil sifting from the seams of the heaviest crate onto the lift floor; pH strip reading 7.9; crate skin 9C against a 21C corridor; EMF 3 mG (normal); window wall 21,300 lux with sunset in 365 min; signature on the delivery slip is a smudge; porter reports it 'smells like a cellar in there'.
incident.ordinary_explanation: The manifest weight of 35 kg each matches the two lighter crates (38 kg, 36 kg), so the 241 kg crate is the anomaly; the black wax, sifting soil and cellar smell are consistent with sealed crates of soil, plants or produce staged for an event, and the 9C skin temperature is consistent with a cold or insulated interior. The smudged signature is consistent with a courier signing in haste. The 3 mG EMF is normal and no creature is described.
incident.summary: Freight delivery of three wooden crates for 'Evening Shift Events, stage plinths' shows one crate at 241 kg against a 35 kg manifest, with black wax on the lids, dark soil sifting from the seams, a 9C skin temperature against a 21C corridor, a smudged signature and a porter's report of a cellar smell. EMF is normal at 3 mG and no creature is described, so the anomaly is confined to the weight, temperature and contents of the crates. The porter plans to park all three in the lounge, which is the closest sector to the freight lift drop point. Severity is low: no entity, no deliberate act and no countermeasure, but the 241 kg crate and its cold, soil-filled interior are unexplained and warrant inspection before it is left unattended in the lounge.

incident.location_detail: Registration desk, badge printer, 3:00 check-in round
incident.evidence_of_threat: Two walk-ins with no pre-registration were admitted to the loft on the word of attendee B-0287 ('they're with my team, let them in'), and two badges were printed for them (Erzsi B., Max S.). The IR fever gate read 16.1C and 16.7C for these two and flagged 'sensor out of range, recalibrate', while the same gate read the next 12 people at 33-34C. The lobby security mirror shows the desk and the queue but not the two walk-ins, and desk staff assumed the glass was dirty.
incident.ordinary_explanation: The gate's low readings are consistent with a miscalibrated or failing sensor rather than genuinely cold subjects, since the same unit immediately returned normal 33-34C readings for the next 12 people. The missing reflection in the lobby security mirror is consistent with the desk's own assumption of dirty glass, and the mirror's field of view covers the desk and queue. The two walk-ins may simply be unregistered teammates of B-0287, and the rule breach is a policy issue rather than a containment event.
incident.summary: Two unregistered walk-ins were badged into the loft on attendee B-0287's say-so. The IR fever gate flagged their temperatures as out of range (16.1C, 16.7C) but then read the next 12 people normally, and the lobby security mirror did not show them, which staff attributed to dirty glass. No creature or hazard is established in the report; the open items are the sensor fault, the mirror gap, and whether the two should be allowed onto the hack floor.

incident.location_detail: first-aid corner, hack floor east, table 22
incident.evidence_of_threat: Three team members (badges B-0377 to B-0379) present separately with fever 38.4C, 38.7C, 39.0C, each rising 0.3C in 20 minutes; itching along forearms; one shaved twice since lunch; heart rate 104-112 bpm. All three ate three portions of rare roast beef at lunch and nothing else. A teammate reports they were scratched 'on a night hike near Muir Woods on Sunday'. All three are repeatedly checking a moon-tracker app (moonrise in 252 min, 20:02, azimuth 54, 93% lit). Window lux 7,300, room 22C.
incident.ordinary_explanation: A shared foodborne illness from undercooked rare roast beef (three portions each, no other food) explains the simultaneous fever, tachycardia and general malaise; the itching and forearm scratching could be dermatologic or contact irritation. The Muir Woods scratch is a plausible mundane source of local skin irritation, and the moon-tracker app checking is consistent with werewolf-themed event culture rather than any actual lunar effect. The 0.3C rise in 20 minutes is consistent with normal fever progression.
incident.summary: Three teammates from table 22 (badges B-0377 to B-0379) separately reported to the first-aid corner of the hack floor east with rising fever (38.4-39.0C, each up 0.3C in 20 min), forearm itching, one shaved twice since lunch, and heart rate 104-112 bpm. All three ate three portions of rare roast beef at lunch and nothing else; a teammate says they were scratched on a night hike near Muir Woods on Sunday. All three are fixated on a moon-tracker app (moonrise in 252 min, 20:02, azimuth 54, 93% lit). Room 22C, window lux 7,300. No creature, spectral or anomalous activity is evidenced; the readings point to a shared foodborne cause plus a mundane scratch, with moon-app checking consistent with event folklore. No deliberate act and no countermeasure required. Severity low: three mildly ill attendees, no injury, no hazard, no containment action needed beyond standard first aid and food-service follow-up on the roast beef.
